title: Property Management & Leasing Basics
originality: All items original to LicensePath. Modeled on the DRE exam blueprint and style only; no actual exam items reproduced.

questions.stem: A property manager normally acts as agent for the:
rationales: Correct. The management agreement ordinarily establishes agency with the owner.
A resident is not automatically the manager's client.
A vendor has a different role.
Recording is unrelated.

questions.stem: An owner says they do not want families with children upstairs. The manager should:
options: Refuse the instruction and escalate the fair-housing concern
rationales: This can be discriminatory.
Correct. The manager cannot implement an unlawful discriminatory instruction.
Changing the channel does not cure the problem.
Different treatment creates further risk.
Selective changes may create discrimination risk.
Correct. Consistency supports lawful, fair operations.
Photos should not drive screening decisions.
The broker must supervise the process.

questions.stem: A resident reports water flowing from a ceiling light fixture. The manager should first:
options: Follow emergency protocol and arrange urgent qualified response
rationales: Delay can worsen immediate danger.
Correct. Potential electrical/water hazards require prompt emergency procedures.
The manager lacks basis to make that assurance.
Diagnosis is outside the ordinary management role.

questions.stem: The best record for a maintenance complaint is a:
options: Timestamped work order with communications and outcome
rationales: A verbal promise may be untraceable.
Correct. A detailed work order creates an auditable factual record.
Social media is not a complete file.
Memory is not a reliable record.

questions.stem: Rent and security deposits should be handled through:
rationales: Personal accounts create control risk.
Correct. Client funds need approved handling and accounting.
Cash drawers are not appropriate controls.
Funds must not be mixed between properties.

questions.stem: A prospect asks for a disability-related exception to a policy. The manager should:
options: Route it through the approved accommodation process
Ask for medical details in public
rationales: Inconvenience alone is not the proper analysis.
Correct. Accommodation requests require the broker's approved fair-housing procedure.
Sensitive information must be handled carefully.
Ignoring it creates risk.
Marketing is unrelated.
Correct. The ledger documents the resident's account activity.
Title is unrelated.
Lending is unrelated.

questions.stem: An owner wants buyers shown an occupied unit whenever convenient. The manager should:
options: Use approved notice/access process and document it
rationales: Keys require controlled access.
Correct. Privacy and entry require the authorized process.
Undocumented entry is risky.
The manager cannot impose that demand.

options: Two-bedroom unit with verified features and availability
rationales: It describes preferred people.
It may discriminate based on familial status.
Correct. It describes the property neutrally.
It references religion/neighborhood composition.

questions.stem: A resident disputes a lease clause. The manager should:
options: Document facts and escalate to broker and appropriate counsel
rationales: Legal interpretation may exceed the role.
Correct. Preserve facts and refer the dispute through authorized channels.
Threats are not legal advice.
Lease changes require authority.

questions.stem: Why should applicant files be secured?
options: They can be shared in group chats
rationales: Correct. Applications often contain identification and financial data.
Marketing is not the main reason.
A lease is a different document.
Group chats can expose private information.

questions.stem: A manager's duty of obedience means following:
rationales: Unlawful instructions must not be followed.
Correct. Agency obedience is bounded by law and authority.
Residents are not automatically the client.
Vendors do not set agency instructions.

questions.stem: Before promising a full security-deposit return, a manager should:
options: Use current authorized process and records
rationales: A promise may be unsupported.
Correct. Deposit treatment is legally sensitive and must follow current authorized procedures.
Vendors do not determine deposit rights.
The lease may be relevant but is not the only source.

questions.stem: A manager sees visible mold-like growth. The best statement is:
options: There is visible growth; qualified evaluation and authorized response are needed
rationales: The manager should not diagnose.
An unsupported assurance is risky.
Correct. It documents observation and routes expertise appropriately.
Concealment is improper.

questions.stem: When exact entry or notice rules are relevant, rely on:
rationales: Old advice may be inaccurate.
Correct. Exact legal requirements must be verified against current authority and approved policy.
Preference cannot override law.
Rumor is not authority.
